summary: Intermittent duplicate function calls when client reconnects over HTTP/2 — idempotency header truncated across frames
description:
Issue summary:
Customers running long-lived streaming sessions over HTTP/2 occasionally observe duplicate executions of downstream function/webhook calls after an in-stream reconnect. The duplicates occur only when the client reconnects within ~3s after a network hiccup and seem correlated with large idempotency header values (base64-encoded blobs) being split across HTTP/2 HEADERS/CONTINUATION frames.

Impact:
- Nimbus Forms reported 5 duplicate webhook executions in the last 48 hours causing duplicate order submissions and triggering billing edge-cases.
- Affects enterprise customers using Python and Go SDKs with streaming + function calling enabled.
- Leads to data integrity issues for customers that rely on at-most-once semantics for external side effects.

Environment:
- Redwood prod us-east-1 (api-gateway fronted by ALB -> http2-enabled proxies -> backend runtime)
- Customer uses Python SDK v1.12.3 (streaming), Go SDK v0.9.1 also observed similar behavior
- Model: gpt-redwood-2-xl; request pattern: streaming chat with function_call = "auto" and idempotency token set by SDK per-session

Steps to reproduce (approximate, intermittent):
1) Start a streaming chat session from the Python SDK with a long idempotency token (~220 bytes base64).
2) Trigger a function call that results in an outbound webhook (customer's endpoint).
3) Introduce a short network interruption (e.g., TCP RST / client reconnect) while the client is still streaming (observed radius: within 1-5 seconds of first function call emission).
4) Client reconnects and resumes the stream. Server accepts the resumed stream and replays the last chunk(s).
5) Downstream webhook receives a second invocation for the same logical function-call id.

Observed logs/attachments (sanitized):
- api-gateway access logs show two POSTs to the webhook endpoint within 1s of each other with different X-Request-Id values.
- Runtime debug trace: idempotency-header present on initial HEADERS but truncated on reconnect HEADERS; header value differs by a suffix of 8-12 bytes.
- Client-side SDK log (Python): "reconnect: resuming stream, sending HEADERS with idempotency-token: <truncated>"

Notes:
- Reproduction rate is low (roughly 0.02% of streams for this customer), but impact is high due to billing and side-effects.
- Hypothesis from Nimbus: internal proxy or ALB is re-chunking headers on reconnect and dropping continuation bytes for very long header values.

Request:
- Investigate whether our HTTP/2 handling path accepts header continuations correctly on resumed streams and if any ingress proxies (ALB / sidecar) truncate long headers across reconnects.
- Determine mitigations (e.g., enforce idempotency token length limit, normalize tokens to a short stable hash at gateway, or adjust SDK to send a compact token).
comments: 2026-03-12 | Aisha Khan (Support): Initial report from Nimbus. Attached sanitized webhook payloads and gateway access logs. Customer requests urgent mitigation options.
2026-03-12 | SRE Triage: Assigned to Benito. Noted correlation with long header sizes. Added labels and requested packet captures from customer network path.

2026-03-13 | Benito Marsh (SRE): Collected ALB logs and tcpdump from internal proxy. Observed HEADERS frame split where CONTINUATION frame never reached runtime in ~3 spurious reconnects. Opened SDK issue to add shorter default session token: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/842
2026-03-13 | Nimbus (customer): Confirmed they can reproduce by forcing a reconnect with large token; willing to test a gateway-side patch or SDK change. Asking about rollback risk.

2026-03-14 | Engineering (Runtime): Noted a rare edge in our HTTP/2 parser where header continuation frames arriving post-stream-resume could be dropped if connection state was not fully rebuilt. Working on a patch to make continuation assembly tolerant to reconnects. ETA for patch: 2026-03-17.

2026-03-14 | Support (Aisha): Suggested interim mitigation: reduce idempotency token length (SDK change) and enable a short-term duplicate-suppression window in the webhook consumer. Customer agreed to test SDK alpha tomorrow.
investigation: Packet capture (internal): shows HEADERS (frame length ~160) followed by CONTINUATION (frame length ~64) during initial stream; on reconnect only HEADERS arrives, CONTINUATION missing due to proxy-level reset.
ALB config review: http2 enabled; no known bug reports, but our sidecar unit tests didn't cover very long header sequences across reconnects.

SDK behavior: current SDKs generate per-session idempotency tokens as base64 of 128 random bytes. This produces headers up to ~172 characters before encoding; some proxies resegment headers differently leading to splitting across frames.
Runtime parser: previously assumed a single HEADERS frame for tokens under 512 bytes; partial parsing logic didn't maintain a continuation buffer across stream-resume boundary.
Customer reproducibility: high when token >= 160 chars and reconnect is forced within 5s. Lower token lengths (<80 chars) did not reproduce duplicates in tests.
root_cause: Edge case in HTTP/2 header continuation handling: when long idempotency headers are split into HEADERS+CONTINUATION frames, a reconnect path could drop continuation frames due to connection/resume state reconstruction in our HTTP/2 pipeline, leading to truncated token being processed as a different idempotency value and causing duplicate downstream function calls.
resolution:
Immediate mitigations: 1) Engineering patched runtime HTTP/2 parser to buffer and assemble CONTINUATION frames across stream-resume states; patch merged to canary on 2026-03-14. 2) Released SDK hotfix to compute a compact token (sha256 hex of random bytes) by default in v1.12.4-alpha to keep header length < 64 chars; link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/842. 3) Support recommended customer deploy a short dedupe window on webhook consumer for 10s until runtime patch fully rolled out.

Rollout notes: patch on canary 2026-03-14; planned gradual rollout to prod us-east-1 on 2026-03-16 after smoke tests. SDK hotfix published as alpha 2026-03-14; GA planned 2026-03-18.

Follow-ups: add integration test for long idempotency headers across reconnects, document recommended max token length in SDK docs, and add monitoring alert for unexpected duplicate function invocations (rate > 0.01% per customer).
resolution_status: Mitigated - patch deployed to canary; customer testing scheduled
notes_for_documentation: Recommend updating SDK docs: 'Idempotency token size recommendations' and guidance to prefer compact tokens or SDK defaults that use hashed representations.
Add runbook entry: 'HTTP/2 continuation frame issues' with steps to collect pcap and ALB logs, and quick mitigation steps.
Add automated test: simulate HEADERS+CONTINUATION across reconnect and assert assembled header equality after resume.
